identity.title: Limits to scalable evaluation at the frontier: LLM as judge won’t beat twice the data

problem.claim: The paper studies how much a small set of high-quality labels can debias a large number of model-based judgments for scalable evaluation.

gap.claim: Existing model-as-judge evaluation can introduce biases, while the achievable limits of debiasing were not established in the supplied abstract.

contributions.claim: Derives a limit on ground-truth-label savings for debiasing model judgments.
Reports that practical sample-size savings are more modest than the theoretical limit.
Reports new observations about evaluation debiasing methods and identifies possible future-work avenues.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their work by studying, in principle, how far debiasing methods can go and by providing a corresponding limit plus empirical observations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that when the judge is no more accurate than the evaluated model, no debiasing method can reduce the required ground-truth labels by more than half.
The authors report empirically that achievable sample-size savings in practice are even smaller than their theoretical limit suggests.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-quality annotations are becoming a bottleneck, motivating scalable evaluation without costly labeling.
Using strong existing models as judges is presented as a cheap alternative, but self-preferencing and other biases can distort comparisons.
The paper studies the principled ceiling on debiasing and reports a maximum twofold reduction in labels under the stated accuracy condition.
The authors report that real-world savings are more modest, especially when evaluating models that may outperform the judge.

source_observation.claim: The abstract states the central limit together with the condition that the judge is no more accurate than the evaluated model, then contrasts it with empirical savings.

lessons.interpretation: Pairing a quantitative claim with its operating condition and a practical comparison makes the scope of the result easier to assess.
lessons.application: State a method or scaling claim alongside its key regime condition, theoretical ceiling, and observed practical outcome.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the relevant conditions or empirical benchmark are not yet defined.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal accuracy model, evaluation task, or assumptions underlying the theoretical limit.
The empirical evaluation's datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical savings are not provided.
